title: 1976 AHSME Problem 3
statement: The sum of the distances from one vertex of a square with sides of length two to the midpoints of each of the sides of the square is

solutions.text:
The two midpoints on sides meeting the chosen vertex are each at distance \(1.\) The other two midpoints have coordinate differences \(2\) and \(1,\) so each is at distance \(\sqrt{2^2+1^2}=\sqrt5.\) The sum is \(2+2\sqrt5.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is E.
hints: Place the chosen vertex at \((0,0)\) and the other vertices at \((2,0),\) \((2,2),\) and \((0,2)\)
Two midpoints are one unit away, while each opposite-side midpoint forms legs \(2\) and \(1\)
